Results.ReviewText: This is a great grill to cook on, and the features for the price is spot on for what I need. However, some real world thoughts that really don't change my 5 star rating are as follows: I ordered extra square legs ($24) to replace the very cheap and badly designed fragile wheel system to make the grill sit on four legs instead of two (with two wheels). The instructions are also lacking details and are poorly made. I wish they could improve that to make setting it up easier and quicker. The packaging was well done, but a simple rip in the other shell from the retail store causer one side panel to get dented.

Results.ReviewText:
The old grill I was replacing had the larger wheels on the right just like the Weber and smaller ones on spindles on the left that made moving it easy.  The place on my patio where I keep the grill is in a place where if assembled as shown, I would have to lift the grill from the right table and DRAG the grill on the fixed feet until it was clear to the point I could move it away from the house.  Not exactly optimal!

I contacted Weber and asked them if I could assemble it with the wheels on the left.  They steadfastly told me it was not recommended to make any changes.  However, when I was putting it together it became clear that all four corners at the bottom where the wheels and feet go were identical, so I put it together with the wheels on the left.  I told Weber that they should make that an option so folks could assemble it to suit their needs.

Weber got all testy with me saying it was dangerous (but didn't say how, because that's impossible) and said it could void my warranty.  PULEEEZE!

For what it's worth, I'm a retired professional firefighter, 30 years.  I understand risk/reward assessments.  There is no way on Earth that doing what I did created a hazard.  In fact, it could be argued that dragging it on the feet to get it away from the house, eventually ruining the feet could create a hazard!

For the life of me, I can't understand why, oh why, Weber is so obtuse!
Results.Title: Assembling The Grill

Results.ReviewText: I've used Weber gas grills since 1985, the Genesis models. My last was wearing out and I saw this model rated highly in Cook's Illustrated magazine. I was concerned it might be too small, but decided to buy it and I'm very pleased I did. The E-325 comes with cast iron grates (I replaced the wire grates on previous units with cast iron) and heats up quickly, evenly, and will run up to 700' no problem. The sear settings work perfectly for cooking game meats while I can cook vegetables at the same time at lower temps on the other burner. Grill size is adequate and more efficient than the Genesis for my uses. The modern design is well thought out with nice features such as silicon bumpers on the lid for quiet, gentle closing, and wheels large enough to move easily. Dropping the side tables makes for a minimal foot print which I had not been concerned about but appreciate now.
Results.Title: Excellent design and function
